clue.text: Caribbean island reversing recent arrest, nominee is claiming

indicators.note: reversing tells you to read the run of letters from right to left
a phrase that claims something holds it inside itself, so the run of letters sits within the clue words

parts.note: read backwards, the letters of these words contain the island's name ending in the first three letters of the last word

explanation.surface: A news item about an island where a nominee is claiming a recent arrest was overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards from the 'nom' of nominee through 'arrest' and into the end of 'recent' to find MONTSERRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Montserrat is a British overseas territory in the Leeward Islands of the West Indies.

clue.text: Sauce Underground worker

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a rich Mexican sauce made with chilli and chocolate
second meaning: a burrowing animal, or a spy planted inside an organisation

explanation.walkthrough: 'Underground worker' suggests a Tube employee or miner; here it is the burrowing animal or a secret agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Mole is both a spicy Mexican chocolate-chilli condiment and a tunnelling mammal or embedded spy.

clue.text: Wins title, wrongly dismissing league's outsiders as "fools"

indicators.note: something done wrongly is done out of order, so the remaining letters are rearranged
to dismiss is to send away, so those letters are taken out of the fodder
outsiders are the people on the edge, so only the first and last letters of the word are meant

parts.note: taken as written
the first and last letters of league

explanation.surface: A team wins a title, and pundits who wrote them off are branded fools.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove L and E from WINSTITLE, then rearrange WINSTIT into NITWITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitwits are silly, foolish people; the plural matches the plural in the clue.

clue.text: Lift going up allows American to enter

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top
entering means going inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: lets is a synonym for allows
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A lift heading upwards lets an American step inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift going up' reads as an elevator; Lift alone is the definition, and 'going up' turns LETS round.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something can mean to pinch it, taking it without permission, which is to steal it.

clue.text: Kid, maybe smallest offspring, protects mum around home

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround and shield it, so one piece holds another

parts.note: the runt is the smallest animal of a litter

indicators.note: around means wrapped about, so the next piece goes inside this one

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A tiny child, the smallest of the family, sheltered by their mother at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Kid looks like a human child, but here it is a young goat, an animal that chews the cud.
explanation.definitionFit: A kid is a young goat, and goats chew the cud, so a kid is an example of a cud-chewing animal.

clue.text: Succeeding to promote area for change

indicators.note: in a down clue, promoting a letter lifts it higher, so it moves to the top of the word

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area
succeeding means coming after, later

explanation.surface: Winning promotion to a new area brings change.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the A out of LATER and raise it to the top of the down entry: LATER becomes ALTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something is to modify it or make it different, the verb sense of change.

clue.text: Great deal of money, mine perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: informal, as in a car that cost a fortune
second meaning: an explosive device, of which a mine is one kind

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' looks like a source of riches such as a gold mine, but it is the explosive kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally something that costs a bomb costs a fortune; a landmine is one sort of explosive device.

clue.text: Natural new grain in ordinary crops, originally

indicators.note: something new has been remade, so the letters take a fresh order
originally points to the start, so only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: O is a standard abbreviation for ordinary
the letters of grain rearranged
the first letter of crops

explanation.surface: Natural farming means new grain among ordinary crops, as originally grown.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic produce is grown without synthetic chemicals, so it is natural in the farming sense.

clue.text: Irritating European group returning to entertain different people

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to take them in, so one piece holds the other
returning means going back, so these letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a mob is a crowd or gang
others are people other than oneself

explanation.surface: An annoying European group that keeps coming back to host foreigners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European group' suggests the EU, but European is just its abbreviation and group a crowd; the reversal covers both before the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bothersome causes annoyance or trouble, so it is irritating; both are adjectives.

clue.text: Articulate Native American facing reminder of the past

indicators.note: to articulate is to pronounce words, so what follows is judged by how it is said

parts.note: the Sioux are a Native American people
a facing is a thin surface layer, a veneer

explanation.surface: An eloquent Native American confronting a memento of history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulate' looks like an adjective for the Native American; it is the sound signal. Said together, Sioux veneer is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A souvenir is a keepsake or memento that brings back memories of a place or event.

clue.text: Unlimited praise for what barista serves up

indicators.note: without limits means without its boundaries, so the first and last letters are lost

parts.note: to flatter is to praise, often excessively

explanation.surface: Lavish compliments for the coffee a barista hands over.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip F and R from the ends of FLATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is espresso with steamed milk, a standard drink made and handed over by coffee-shop staff.

clue.text: This writer felt satisfied penning If

indicators.note: penning means enclosing as in a pen, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to meet a demand is to satisfy it
as in 'as though' meaning 'as if'

explanation.surface: A poet recalls the satisfaction of writing Kipling's poem If.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If' with its capital looks like Kipling's poem; it is just the word. Methought is an archaic form meaning 'I thought'.
explanation.definitionFit: Methought is the old-fashioned form of 'it seemed to me', so it means the setter thought or felt.

clue.text: Female departing country amid regret quits HMRC previously

indicators.note: something departing leaves, so that letter comes out of the word

parts.note: a Nordic country
F is the abbreviation for female

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: to rue is to regret
to be quits is to be even, owing nothing

explanation.surface: A woman leaves her homeland, sorry to quit her job at the tax office.
explanation.walkthrough: HMRC (His Majesty's Revenue and Customs) is the UK tax authority, formed in 2005 by merging the Inland Revenue with Customs and Excise.
explanation.definitionFit: Before HMRC existed, the British body collecting income tax was called the Inland Revenue.

clue.text: Suspect a nastiness in French barman

indicators.note: as an adjective suspect means dubious or not genuine, so the letters are not in their true order

parts.note: the ten letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Suspicion that a French bartender harbours a nasty streak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barman' looks like a bartender, but here a bar is a unit of music, so a bar man is a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Camille Saint-Saëns was a French composer, a writer of musical bars, hence the playful bar man.

clue.text: Promising to secure million for Republican is arrogant

indicators.note: to secure something is to take hold of it, so the new letter is brought into the word
one thing for another means swapping it in place of the other letter

parts.note: assuring means promising or pledging
M is the abbreviation for million
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Pledging to raise a million for a Republican campaign looks arrogant.
explanation.walkthrough: In ASSURING, the R is swapped for an M.
explanation.definitionFit: An assuming person takes too much for granted and is presumptuous, a sense close to haughty or overbearing.

clue.text: Financial backing from Canada supports artist adding track

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: Claude Monet, the French Impressionist painter

indicators.note: the backing of a word is its rear, so only the final letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of Canada
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Canadian financial backing for a painter as he expands a racetrack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Financial backing' reads as a single phrase, but backing belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Monetary describes matters relating to money or currency, the same field as financial.

clue.text: Flipping sensible limits court establishes by law

indicators.note: limits are the edges round something, so these letters wrap around the next piece
flipping something over turns it the other way round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: sane means sensible, rational
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A frustrated complaint that sensible limits set by a court are being imposed by statute.
explanation.definitionFit: A legislature enacts a measure when it passes it into law, making it an Act.

clue.text: Second son wearing suit arrives at plant

indicators.note: something being worn is wrapped in it, so these pieces go inside the next one

parts.note: clubs is one of the four suits in a pack of cards
a mo is a moment, a second
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A second son, dressed in a suit, turns up at a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant looks like an industrial site in the surface; it is the botanical sense. 'Suit' is a card suit, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Club moss is a low evergreen spore-bearing plant related to ferns, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Observing husband is lacking in love

indicators.note: when something is lacking it is missing, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: in tennis, love means a score of nothing
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Noticing that a husband is lacking in affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' is the tennis score of zero; take the H out of NOTHING.
explanation.definitionFit: Noting something means taking notice of it or remarking on it, the same as observing it.

clue.text: Tourist, one who's grounded?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a day-..., someone on a short pleasure trip
second meaning, whimsical: someone who stumbles ends up on the ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounded' suggests a punished teenager or a plane kept on the tarmac; the question mark flags the playful sense of one who trips and falls.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripper is a sightseer on an outing, and literally also anyone who trips over and lands on the floor.

clue.text: Trite statement by gutless animal charity

indicators.note: with its guts removed only the outer shell of the word remains

parts.note: the first and last letters of animal
a truism is a self-evident, hackneyed remark

explanation.surface: A cliché from a spineless animal welfare charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal charity' reads as one organisation, but charity alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Altruism is selfless concern for others, which is the older, wider sense of charity as benevolence.

clue.text: Where to find Gary, popular with royalty once

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
Diana, Princess of Wales, formerly part of the royal family

explanation.surface: Someone called Gary who was once a favourite of the royals.
explanation.walkthrough: Gary sounds like a person; it is a steel city on Lake Michigan.
explanation.definitionFit: Gary is an industrial city in the American Midwest state, located in its northwest corner.

clue.text: Circumventing directors, one may face carpeting

parts.note: skirting means going around, avoiding
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: An employee who goes around the board of directors risks a reprimand.
explanation.walkthrough: A carpeting is British slang for a dressing-down; here it is literal floor carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirting board is the wooden strip along the base of a wall, which sits directly beside the floor covering.

clue.text: Nordhausen in Thuringia inspiring Beethoven's final symphony

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the clue words take the answer inside them

parts.note: the last letter of the first word, all of the second and the first two of the third

explanation.surface: A German town in Thuringia that inspired the composer's last symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: Thuringia is a German state, which makes a Beethoven setting feel natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven completed nine symphonies, and the last, the Choral, is known simply as his Ninth.

clue.text: Extremely deficient grid being refined

indicators.note: deficient at the extremes means missing its ends, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a lattice is a grid of crossed strips

explanation.surface: A badly flawed grid being polished up.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove L and E from the ends of LATTICE. Attic with a capital refers to ancient Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic style, from classical Athens, means elegant and pure, so it describes something polished or cultivated.

clue.text: Props close to actors on set knocked over

indicators.note: knocked over means toppled, so in a down entry the letters are turned upside down
in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it
the close of a word is its end, so only its last letter is used

parts.note: the last letter of actors
to set is to gel, as a jelly does

explanation.surface: Stage props near the actors get knocked over on the set.
explanation.walkthrough: Props and set suggest theatre, but props are supports and set means solidify.
explanation.definitionFit: Legs are supports, such as the legs propping up a table, so they serve as props.

clue.text: Language of hate, hard to ignore, person broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is, so the letters are spread into a new order
what you ignore is left out, so that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hate speech from a person that is hard to ignore when it goes out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the H from HATE and rearrange ATE with PERSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an invented international tongue devised by Zamenhof in 1887.

clue.text: City skill reflected in draw

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the letters run back to front

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A city's artistic talent shown in a drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: The City, capitalised, is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace is to copy a drawing through thin paper, so in that sense it means to draw.

clue.text: "Order!" Speaker's requested

indicators.note: a speaker's words are heard, not read, so the clue word is taken by its sound

parts.note: sought is a synonym for requested

explanation.surface: The Speaker of the Commons calls 'Order!' as requested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order! Order!' is the famous cry of the Commons Speaker, so the speaker seems to be that official. In non-rhotic British speech, sought and sort sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To sort things is to arrange them in sequence, which is putting them in order.

clue.text: Doctors in Spain, shy around nurses in charge

indicators.note: around suggests letters thrown about, so the preceding words are rearranged
to nurse something is to hold it close, so these letters take the next piece inside

parts.note: the eight letters rearranged
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Bashful doctors in Spain hanging around nurses who are in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurses' sits naturally beside doctors in the surface, but here it is a verb meaning holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicians are medical practitioners, the formal name for doctors of medicine.
